name: Blaziken
flavor_text: Kindle your fighting spirit with Blaziken’s Firestarter ability to acceleate energy into play, and then snipe with Blaziken ex!

name: Crobyss
flavor_text: Use Crobat's Flutter Trick to stunt your opponents setup while slowly attaching psychic energy to your Pokemon for big end-game Mystic Waters from Gorebyss!

name: Gardevoir
flavor_text: Slow and steady wins the race! You may have a lot of Pokemon to get fully set up, but once everything is in order you can easily steamroll your opponent!

name: Mediturnette
flavor_text: Gotta go fast! Use the speedy Team Magma engine to spread damage with Groudon and take big KOs before your opponent even sets up!

name: Swampert
flavor_text: Set up multiple Swampert on the bench to power up Swampert ex’s Hyper Pump to take giant 1 hit KOs on most Pokemon!

name: Team Aqua
flavor_text: This deck may be even faster than Magma! Use Electrike's Self Charge to power up an extremely quick turn Manectric Thunderspark! Kyogre and Cacturne add more powerful options to this extremely speedy package.

name: Team Magma
flavor_text: Gotta go fast! Use the speedy Team Magma engine to spread damage with Groudon and take big KOs before your opponent even sets up!

name: Walrein
flavor_text: This is a pretty slow format, and this deck makes it even slower! Tank hits with Walrein, and once  it takes damage, heal with Milotic and do it all over again!

name: Armaldo
flavor_text: Get ready to mulligan! This deck plays only a single basic Pokemon, and hopes to use the effect of Strange Cave to put Anorith or Aerodactyl straight onto the bench. Once you go through the hassle of getting an Armaldo ex set up, you can tank and heal your way through your opponent!

name: Bombtar
flavor_text: KABOOM! Use Electrode ex's Exploding energy Poke-Power to accelerate tons of special energy from your discard pile onto your Dark Tyranitar to launch massive Grind attacks! Though each Electrode gives your opponent two prizes, you can use this to your advantage with Pow! Hand extension and scramble energy.

name: Camler
flavor_text: Stop your opponent in their tracks with Stantler's Push Away to remove important trainer cards, then spread damage with Camerupt's split bomb to pick off their most important Pokemon!

name: Delta Flygon
flavor_text: Set up Flygon ex with Flygon's Delta Supply power, and then spread damage and continually move it however you want with the Pidgeot and Absol ex combo!

name: Gardevoir
flavor_text: Swap energy between multiple Gardevoir ex to tank big hits while putting Imprison counters to completely stop your opponent from using Poke-Powers!

name: LBS
flavor_text: The gold standard for this format, efficiently use Castform as an energy while getting extra attachments with Blastoise ex's Energy Rain to use high energy cost attacks on a variety of Pokemon!

name: Nidoqueen
flavor_text: Set up extremely tanky single prize Nidoqueens to poison your opponent and stop them from using Poke-Powers, while you set up your board for huge Power Lariat attacks!

name: Rayler
flavor_text: Tord Reklev's favorite RS-PK deck. Run your opponent out of resources with Stantler and energy removal, before coming in with giant and efficient attacks from Rayquaza ex to finish the game!

name: Ludicargo
flavor_text: A single prize deck that doesn't rely on Pidgeot, you can effectively use Battle Frontier to slow down your opponents while stacking your deck with Magcargo's Smooth Over. Ludicolo's Swing Dance lets you immediately draw it, so it's basically Pidgeot!

name: Medinette
flavor_text: Shut down your opponent's powers with Medicham ex and spread damage with Pure Power. When a Pokemon takes a hit, you can then use Bannette ex's Shady move to send the damage right back and hit hard with a Shadow Chant!

name: Mewtric
flavor_text: The deck Jason K used to win his first of three World Championships, this box deck hopes to set up a Mew ex anc Copy Manectric ex's disconnect to disrupt your opponent and have answers for almost any situation while using Holon's Magneton as Double Rainbow energy!

name: Rai-Eggs
flavor_text: A rogue deck which hope to lock your opponent out of using Poke-Powers with Cessation crystal and spread damage with your powerful single prizers. Effectively use Scramble Energy to take multiple prize turns while your opponent is left unable to respond!

name: Amphysnow
flavor_text: Spread damage with Abomasnow’s Snow Play attack, and then use Ampharos’s Damage Bind Poke-Body to lock your opponenet out of Poke-Powers!

name: Cursegar
flavor_text: Trainer lock your opponent with Spiritomb or Gastly’s attack, allowing you to set up the hyper-efficient Gengar, able to spread damage and take KO’s on your opponent’s support Pokemon!

name: Flyterra
flavor_text: Typically slow to set up, but don’t be fooled by its pace! Once set up, Torterra Lv. X can gust weaker Pokemon and fully heal itself with Giga Drain, or even mill your opponent’s deck with Flygon’s Poke-Body!

name: Gardevoir Gallade
flavor_text: Largely considered the strongest deck of all time, this variant uses Gardevoir to lock your opponent and powerful Stage 2 tech Pokemon like Machamp to deal with its poorer matchups!

name: Gyarados
flavor_text: Who needs energy? Discard Magikarp and use Gyarados’s Tail Revenge for free to make your opponents run away with their tail tucked!

name: Healix
flavor_text: The name says it all. Fill your discard pile with energy and use Energy Stream to build up big attacks while healing damage with Blissey. Once set up, you can continually attach up to four special Metal Energy and tank even the biggest hits while swinging back just as hard!

name: Hippowdon
flavor_text: Tank, heal, and ramp energy with Hippowdon! Build up energy with Save Sand for a powerful Groudquake, and reset the Game with Hippowdon Lv.X’s Sand Reset!

name: Jumpluff
flavor_text: Jumpluff mya be small, but there are strength in numbers. Fill your bench and attack for big damage with Mass Attack!

name: Luxchomp
flavor_text: The king of 2010, Luxchomp has tools for every mathcup! Use Luxray GL Lv.X’s Bright look to gust and KO weaker Pokemon, or snipe them with Garchomp C Lv.X’s Dragon Rush!

name: Regigigas
flavor_text: We demand a sacrifice! Set up Regigigas Lv.X, and then use its Sacrifice Poke-Power to KO your own Pokemon to heal and power up your own!

name: Sablelock
flavor_text: Force yourself to go first with Sableye, giving you a great chance of donking your opponent with Overeager! If that fails, use Impersonate to set up a board of Garchomp and Honchkrow to snipe your opponent's important Pokemon!

name: Shuppet Donk
flavor_text: Use Shuppet’s Fade out to continually reuse Plus Powers and Expert Belt, taking huge KOs even on the first turn, leading to either quick victory or even quicker defeat!

name: Magneboar
flavor_text: An unexpected world champion with multiple stage 2 lines, set up Emboar to power up Magnezone for Lost Burns every turn!

name: Megazone
flavor_text: Get ready to ask “Cards in hand?” every turn! Match hand sizes to attack for free with Yanmega while setting up Magnezone for a big finishing attack!

name: Megazord
flavor_text: Individually they may not be strong, but together they are mighty! A collection of the strongest and most efficient attackers in the format; Donphan for big damage early, Yanmega for sniping, and Zoroark for copying any useful attack your opponent may want to use!

name: Reshiphlosion
flavor_text: One of the most aggressive decks, turbo energy into your discard with Ninetales, then accelerate them with Typhlosion to repeatedly attack with Reshiram!

name: Sharpedo
flavor_text: Strip your opponent's hand of resources with Sharpedo and Weavile, while setting up  a bench full of strong attackers to  Do the Wave for big damage! If you opponent treis to run and hide from your onslaught, Mandibuzz lets you easily chase their wekening Pokemon!.

name: The Truth
flavor_text: This deck broke the meta, and now it will break your will to live! Item lock your opponent and heal infinitely before finishing with Zekrom and Entei & Raikou Legend!

name: Tyranitar Prime
flavor_text: Though quite difficult to set up, Tyranitar is hard to take down with strong attacks and massive HP. Serperior gives you even more effective HP and also negates the downside of Darkness Howl damaging your bench.

name: ZPS
flavor_text: Pachirisu lets you attach extra energy from your hand, and Shaymin lets you move it however you like! Use this to set up multiple Zekrom early and keep swinging before your opponent can even set up.

name: Big Basics
flavor_text: High HP Basics such as Landorus EX and Cobalion EX use efficient attacks to quickly overwhelm your opponent!

name: Blastoise
flavor_text: Use Blastoise’s Deluge ability to stack water energy on Black Kyurem EX to unleash a powerful 200 damage with Black Ballista!

name: Darkrai Garb
flavor_text: Attach a tool to Garbodor to lock your opponent out of their abilities and use Darkrai EX’s Night Spear attack combined with the dual threat of Hynotoxic laser to precisely spread damage to your opponent’s board!

name: Darkrai Sableye
flavor_text: Jason K's third World's win, this deck abuses the fact that the format was filled with extremely strong item cards like Dark Patch and Hypnotoxic Laser in conjuction with Sableye's Junk Hunt to slowly run your opponent out of resources. Double Keldeo EX lets you avoid the opponent's status conditions, and Darkrai EX is one of the best attackers in the format!

name: Flareon
flavor_text: Turbo through your deck and discard as many Pokemon as possible to power up Flareon’s Vengence attack and do heavy damage for one energy card! Terrakion and Landorus give you good attacking options while you power up Flareon.

name: Fluffy Chomp
flavor_text: Life Dew prevents your opponent from taking prizes while you set up powerful single prize Garchomps that disrupt your opponent's sepcial energy! Boost their damage with altaria to take big knockouts while stunting your opponent's setup.

name: Gothgor
flavor_text: This deck may have one of the biggest drop-offs from Nationals to worlds ever. This powerful paralysis and item lock is easily shut down by double Keldeo EX!

name: Sporeprise
flavor_text: Poison, confusion, and sleep, oh my! Gust with Ninetales and inflict status conditions with Amoongus, then devolve and do it again! Victini EX serves as a big closer to take your final prizes after you're finished inflicting status!

name: Ray Eels
flavor_text: Eelektrik’s Dynamotor ability lets you accelerate energy from your discard, allowing you to repeatedly fire off Rayquaza EX’s Dragon Burst attack for massive damage!

name: Shift Gear
flavor_text: Klingklang’s Shift Gear ability lets you move Metal energy however you like, allowing you to heal your Cobalion EX with max potion and keep attacking with Steel Bullet!

name: Team Plasma
flavor_text: Lugia EX can take extra prizes, meaning Deoxys EX’s Power Connect ability boosting its damage can lead to devastating 3 prize tuns!

name: Terrakion Garb
flavor_text: Terrakion EX is big and hits hard, while Garbodor locks your opponent out of their abilities.  Pump-Up Smash lets you keep setting up Terrakion while float stone lets you easily pivot bewteen them!

name: Greninja BREAK
flavor_text: Do you like saying “If only I hadn’t bricked, I’m so unlucky”? This is the deck for you! It works 100% of the time, 50% of the time!

name: Manectric Garb
flavor_text: Quickly attach a tool to Garbodor and use M Manectric EX’s Turbo Bolt to set up powerful attackers while locking your opponent out of their abilities!

name: Mega Audino
flavor_text: This supposed “Night March Beater” actually has a pretty poor matchup if your opponent knows what they’re doing!

name: Mega Sceptile
flavor_text: Using only 4 basic Pokemon, this deck is the epitome of tank and heal. Use M Sceptile EX to both accelerate energy and heal damage from your bench!

name: Night March
flavor_text: Compress your battles by discarding Pokemon with the Night March attack, allowing Joltik and Pumpkaboo to swing for huge knockouts as soon as turn 1!

name: Rainbow Road
flavor_text: Use a pokemon for each color of the rainbow and stack your bench full of dual type pokemon to do massive damage with Xerneas’ Rainbow Force attack!

name: Toady Bats
flavor_text: Use Seismitoad EX to item lock your opponent while Crobat and Golbat can sneakily take KOs by spreading damage!

name: Trevenant
flavor_text: Use Phantump’s Ascension to evolve into Trevenant turn 1, and then get to Tree Slammin’, spreading damage while item locking your opponent!

name: Vespiquen Yveltal
flavor_text: Use Yveltal to power up a Vespiquen and easily counter the opposing Night March and Trevenant strategies while preparing a powerful Bee Revenge attack!

name: Zygarde Plume
flavor_text: Use Forest of Giant plants to set up Vileplume Turn 1 and the use Zygarde EX to tank and heal and outlast your opponent!

name: Buzzgarb
flavor_text: Quickly rush your opponent with powerful single prize attacker Buzzwole, and punish them for using abilities and Item cards with Weavile and Garbodor!

name: BuzzRoc
flavor_text: Early game aggression from Buzzwole and consistent gust from Lycanroc’s Bloodthirty Eyes ability makes this a difficult deck to beat!

name: Dusk Mane Necrozma
flavor_text: In theory, Magnezone powers up Dusk Mane to do crazy damage. In practice, you Steven’s Advice and then don’t have enough energy.

name: Empoleon
flavor_text: Slow to set up, but efficient to keep going, Empoleon can do upwards of 180 damage for one energy attachment!

name: Garchomp
flavor_text: One of my homebrew decks, power up Grachomp and use Lucario to search Cynthia each turn for massive damage with Royal Blades!

name: GardySwampTales
flavor_text: Rack up energy on your Gardevoir GX with Secret Spring to do nearly infinite damage with Infinite Force!

name: Granbull
flavor_text: Keep you hand low to use Granbull’s All Out each turn for maximum damage when you have no cards in your hand!

name: Lost March
flavor_text: Sacrifice your own Pokemon to the Lost Zone to power up Jumpluff and Natu’s Lost March attack to take huge KOs!

name: Malamar
flavor_text: Continuously recover your energy with Malamar’s Psychic Recharge to lauch massive attacks with Necrozma GX!

name: Sceptile
flavor_text: You may not be able to do lots of damage, but that doesn’t matter when you can heal anything done back to you!

name: Steelix Stall
flavor_text: Do people hate you? Well, after playing this deck there won’t be any question! Remove your opponent’s energy and sponge attacks with Steelix to mill your opponent!

name: Vikaray
flavor_text: Stack energy on your board with Vikavolt to build up damage for Rayquaza GX’s Dragon Break attack!

name: White Kyurem
flavor_text: Be small! Swing Big! Loop White Kyurem attacks with Wishful baton to after powering up with Arceus to swing for 160 each turn!

name: ZoroGlaceon
flavor_text: Ability lock your opponent as early as the first turn with Glaceon and draw through your deck with Zoroark!

name: ZoroDeciTales
flavor_text: Set up Decidueye GX and spread damage with Feather Arrow while attacking with Alolan Ninetales GX to take devastating multi-prize turns!

name: ZoroRoc
flavor_text: Consistency defined. Draw cards with Trade, gust with Lycanroc, and swing for big damage with Weavile.

name: Ability Reshizard
flavor_text: Utilize powerful abilities and  the supporter Welder to quickly set up and do massive damage with Reshiram & Charizard GX’s Double Blaze GX attack!

name: Baby Blowns
flavor_text: Use Welder and the variety of Fire support items to accumulate fire energy in your hand to take big KOs with Blacephalon’s Fireball Circus attack!

name: Fossil Box
flavor_text: Pokemon Research lab lets you cheat out Stage 1 Fossil Pokemon, which means you can quickly power up the strong single prize attacker Rampardos!

name: Gardeon
flavor_text: Pair Gardevoir & Sylveon GX with Green’s Exploration to use powerful disruption and healing cards to outlast your opponent!

name: NagQuag
flavor_text: Naganadel’s Charge Up and Quagsire’s Wash Out Ability give the opportunity to quickly accelerate water energy from your discard and power up your active Pokemon!

name: Pikarom
flavor_text: Use Tapu Koko and Thunder Mountain to attack with Pikachu & Zekrom GX on the first turn, setting up for a powerful Tag Bolt GX Attack!

name: ADP
flavor_text: Use Starbirth to search for any 2 cards, then take away your opponent’s hand and abilities with Marnie and Path to the Peak!

name: Mew VMAX
flavor_text: Draw a bajillion cards with Genesect, and then do as much damage as you want with Mew. Go fast, draw cards, and hit hard. I hate this deck.

name: Palkia VStar
flavor_text: Palkia is one of the most efficient attackers in the metagame, and Inteleon lets you search just about anything, so its no wonder this was the deck to beat.

name: Urshifu
flavor_text: Spread damage with Urshifu and search whatever you want with Inteleon and Octillery, all to set up to take an extra turn with Medicham’s Yoga Loop!

name: Colorless Lugia
flavor_text: Do your best to get 2 Archeops in the discard so you can use Lugia’s Summoning Star to immediately put them both on the bench to accelerate powerful Special Energy Cards!

name: Gardevoir
flavor_text: The queen of comebacks! Get psychic energy in the discard to use Garevoir ex’s Psychic Embrace to load up powerful attackers like Baby Gardevoir or Zacian V!

name: Lost Box Kyogre
flavor_text: Turbo through your deck with Comfey and Radiant Greninja to spread with Sableye, and then set up for a big Kyoger Aqua Storm for 4 prizes on the last turn!

name: Lost Tina
flavor_text: Roxanne Path wins games. The least consistent lost zone deck, but its power and disruption are unrivaled!

name: Mew VMAX
flavor_text: Use one of the most broken draw engines ever to draw anything you need exactly when you need it!

name: Miraidon
flavor_text: Hop on this future bike and pray your generators hit! Go fast, and if you every get stuck, Judge path is pretty good!

name: Rapid Strike
flavor_text: Spreading damage is the name of the game! Pick off the low HP Pokemon with Inteleon and set up for big multi-porize turns with Urshifu!

name: Sablezard
flavor_text: Stop and select the flowers as you build towards powerful Sableye spreads, and once you’ve lulled your opponent into a false sense of security, swing for 250 with one energy with Radiant Charizard!
